provenance.status: BOOTSTRAP - NOT a measured 3-max fixed point. Placeholder for M0/M1 only; M2 replaces it with a measured self-play fixed point and every corpus labelled under this file must be relabelled.
provenance.derivation: 3-max settles as a sum of three independent pairwise heads-up comparisons (contract R4). The Fantasyland term therefore enters ONCE PER PAIR, so the constant the scoring kernel consumes is a PER-PAIR value, while the hand-level worth of entering Fantasyland is the sum over both opponents. v0 takes the heads-up per-pair value unchanged (9.6, configs/fl_ev_regular_v4_selfplay.json), which makes the hand total 19.2 - the anchor named in the design note.
provenance.units_warning: The design note's headline number 19.2 is the HAND TOTAL, not the kernel input. Feeding 19.2 to the per-pair kernel would double the Fantasyland term for every label in the cascade. load_fl_ev_3max() rejects any file whose fl_ev_hand_total is not opponents_per_player times fl_ev, which is what makes that mistake loud instead of silent.
provenance.known_bias_direction: Unestablished. Two effects push opposite ways and neither is measured: entering Fantasyland is paid by two opponents (raises the total), but the entry hand also risks fouling against two opponents and the 3-max deck is 51/52 dealt, which changes both the entry rate and what a Fantasyland hand can find (direction unknown). Do not assume 19.2 is a floor or a ceiling.
provenance.predecessor_units: per_pair (heads-up has exactly one pair, so the HU file's value is simultaneously the per-pair value and the hand total)
provenance.replacement_plan: M2: sensitivity probe at +/-30% to find which streets are robust, then a self-play fixed point using the closed-form crossing V* = (V0 - slope*x0)/(1 - slope) that the HU v3/v4 adoptions used. Naive iteration is not to be used: the HU map's slope is negative (-0.144) and iterates alternate.

source: Bootstrap constant for the 3-max track, created 2026-08-12 alongside the M0 game core. Carries no measurement of its own.
